To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the methanogenic community is stable under aerated soil condition for 1 year in paddy-upland field soil.

the abundance of mcrA gene transcripts of methanogenic communities in a paddy field soil decreased by over three order of magnitude after 3 years of uplands conversion, but the composition of active methanic communities remained similar.
a prolonged non-flooded period decreased mcrA transcription of the active methanogenic community in the paddy-upland rotation field soil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of methano-gens in paddy-upland rotation fields and the effects of prolonged non-flooded periods on the active methano-genic archaeal communities.
the stability of methanic archaea community in paddy field.
the stability of methano-genic archaeal community in a paddy field under upland conditions and provides insight into the mechanisms of methanogenic community stability in paddy fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a methanogenic archaeon community is able to survive in upland soils for a long time.
a prolonged non-flooded period (more than 1 years) in paddy fields affects the transcription of mcrA gene of the active methanogenic community.
the mcrA gene transcript levels of methanogenic archaebacteria in paddy fields decrease upon long-term upland cultivation, but that the composition of the active community is stable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the active methanogenic community in paddy field soil is stable under aerated soil condition, and the mcrA transcription of this community is affected by prolonged non-flooded period, which may be longer than 1-year.
the methanogenic community of a paddy-up land rotational field was stable during a prolonged non-flooded period, and the community composition was similar to that in a paddy field.
the stability of the methanogenic community in the paddy-upland field is affected by a prolonged period of drainage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mcrA transcript level of the methanogenic community in paddy-upland rotation field is affected by prolonged non-flooded period, longer than one year.

mcrA transcript level in methanogenic archaeon is affected by the prolonged non-flooded period in the paddy-upland soil, but the composition of methanogenic community was similar to that in the paddy field soil.

the active methanogenic community in the rotational paddy field was similar to that in the control plot, but the mcrA gene transcript level decreased after 2 year of upland conversion, suggesting that unknown mechanisms maintain methanogenic archaeae in paddy fields for up to 1 year after the onset of upland conversion.
